svg.title: What a passing FlashProve check establishes
svg.desc: Notebook diagram showing commit once, prove per reply, check on CPU, and yes or within limits verdict, with a note listing what stays outside the proof.

g.text: commit · prove · check · verdict — and what stays outside
proof rides along with each reply:
~17 s on 24 threads; weights never seen
commitment ID: from a party you trust,
NOT from the server being checked
can't judge the limits? accept only exact-match
II. What a PASS does not say
integer-quantized weights pinned by the commitment,
these exact tokens, under the stated policy,
everything below this line is outside
provider chooses what to commit to
that the output is correct or safe
binds output to weights, not to truth
the surrounding app is not covered
what else the hardware was doing
Soundness: how narrowly is it proved?
Pr[ Lean verifier accepts a false claim ]
q = hash queries · random-oracle model · exact-match only
only the Lean verifier is proved; the C++ verifier and
CUDA prover are tested against it, not proved
PASS = these tokens came from THESE committed
only if the commitment ID is trusted.
vendor-measured figures · research prototype, not deployed
